text:
ana: Quick heads-up — ran a focused profiling pass this morning on the p95 SLO-driven batcher with the new token-balance prefetch heuristic. Posting top-level numbers and a short log excerpt. Looking for opinions on changing queue policy from size-based to weight-based for route/tier tokens.

miguel: thx. can you paste the p95 before/after?

ana: oops typo, ana. before: 218ms p95 for web-search route (prod, gold tier). after: 172ms p95. 15% tail improvement on roaming/longer seq windows. median unchanged (~32ms).

rachel: nice. did cost change? tokens/sec or gpu-util?

ana: cost impact small — token throughput increased slightly due to more aggressive prefetch (kernel warmups reduce per-token cpu), overall GPU util +3%, estimated cost delta +1.2% for that pool.

samir: curious about KV cache hit rates — did prefetch bump cold miss rate because we pull prefixes earlier?

ana: good call. KV hit-rate: baseline 87% -> 84% after change on that route. Misses concentrated on long-tail new-conversation traffic. I added a buffer to avoid prefetching for <3-message contexts.

miguel: can you share the short log snippet for the batch formation? a few lines are enough.

ana: sure — paste: ```
[2118765433] batch-formed route=web-search tier=gold tokens_target=240 actual_tokens=238 kernel=triton_v2 prefetch=enabled kv_prefetch=buffered decisions=[route_score=0.87,wait_ms=12]
[2118765440] kernel-swap triggered: triton_v2 -> triton_v2_q4 at queue_watermark=180 reason=latency_surge
[2118765455] batch-split: large-request id=0x7f tokens=1024 -> split into 4 microbatches
```

rachel: that kernel-swap line worries me — why did it switch to q4 quant path? that usually happens for cost fallback, not perf.

ana: swap triggered by the fallback governor; we set a rule to prefer quantized kernels when batch size >200 to reduce OOMs. But profiler shows triton_v2_q4 has worse cold-start p95 for seq>512 — maybe our kernel selection thresholds are inverted.

samir: so tradeoff is smaller p95 for common cases vs huge regression on big sequences. did you capture call counts by seq length?

ana: yes. call distribution: seq<=256: 78% of calls, 256<seq<=1024: 18%, >1024: 4%. The p95 regression is dominated by the 4% bucket but has outsized tail impact.

miguel: suggested quick fix: add a route-tier override: never auto-quantize for sequences >512 on gold tier. keep quant path for bronze.

rachel: agree. plus we should tweak queue policy: weight-based where weight = tokens_remaining * tier_multiplier, so high-tier short requests get prioritized over large cheap bronze batches.

samir: on batching heuristics: can we limit prefetch to avoid chasing cold prefixes? maybe add an LRU TTL on prefetched entries and only prefetch when KV access entropy < threshold.

ana: implementing TTL 30s + entropy check (shannon < 1.2) — ran a quick A/B; that recovers KV hit-rate to 86% and keeps p95 at 175ms. acceptable.

deploy-bot: deploy started for experiment/kv-prefetch-ttl-30 (canary: 3 nodes)

miguel: once canary stabilizes we should run a 24h window and compute p95 by route & tier and produce a diff heatmap. also include per-kernel cold-warm p95 samples.

rachel: note to self — QA should replay long-seq traces to validate no functional regressions from kernel path changes.

ana: action items: (1) add route-tier override for quantization thresholds (ana), (2) implement LRU TTL + entropy gate for prefetch (ana+samir), (3) change queue policy prototype to weight-based and run 6h canary (miguel), (4) generate heatmap (rachel). I'll open a follow-up thread with the canary link and perf dashboards.

samir: +1. also add a small synthetic test that forces seq>1024 to catch kernel-swap regressions earlier.

miguel: cool. thanks — nice improvement overall :chart_with_upwards_trend:

ana: thanks all. will update when canary finishes.
